title: The man born blind. Part 3
scripture_text: ‘’As he went along, he saw a man blind from birth. His disciples asked him, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?” “Neither this man nor his parents sinned,”said Jesus, “but this happened so that the works of God might be displayed in him. As long as it is day, we must do the works of him who sent me. Night is coming, when no one can work. While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.” After saying this, he spit on the ground, made some mud with the saliva, and put it on the man’s eyes. “Go,” he told him, “wash in the Pool of Siloam” (this word means “Sent”). So the man went and washed, and came home seeing.’’
devotional:
Jesus response to the disciple’s question

Before we look at what Jesus said to his disciples it is important to note that the answer he gave was not intended to feed their curiosity, increase their knowledge or to make them more theologically sound. The answer was to challenge their prejudice, change their attitudes and motivate them to practical care.

Jesus challenged their understanding of suffering.

For the Jew suffering was always related to sin, but in this passage Jesus relates it to the revelation of God. This was something these disciples had never heard before. How could God be glorified through suffering?

The interesting thing is that Jesus viewed his own suffering as a means of bringing glory to God.

‘All sufferings are opportunities for God to be glorified, irrespective of the cause. If our suffering is indeed a punishment for sin, then it becomes an occasion for repentance and thus the manifestation of God's grace as we are restored to fellowship with God. If our suffering is not a direct punishment for sin, then it is something God allows to happen in our lives, usually for reasons beyond our knowing, which nevertheless can help us die to self and find our true life in God. God does not allow anything to enter our lives that is not able to glorify him by drawing us into deeper intimacy with him and revealing his glory.’ IVP commentary.

Jesus challenged their lack of practical concern for the man.

‘We must work the works of him who sent me while it is day; night is coming when no one can work.’ He did not say, “I must work the works of him who sent me,” but ‘we must work’. What is the work Jesus is referring to? The work is the gracious, kind, compassionate, non-judgmental accepting attitude that Jesus showed towards the blind man, the work of accepting the outcast. The heart attitude that is expressed in the work Jesus spoke of, is the opposite of the heart attitude that was expressed in the disciple’s question. Sometimes we over spiritualise the ‘work’ of God. We see it as some secret, mysterious thing that comes to us through some special revelation, when, all it is, is simply showing love and compassion to those we meet every day. An unhealthy and unhelpful interest in theology will prevent a person from showing compassion; a proper understanding of theology will motivate a person to do deeds of practical compassion.

The Greek word for work is ‘ergazomai" which has these possible meanings (from Lexicon of New Testament Greek):

To work, or labour, to do work.

To trade, to make gains by trading, "to do business".

To do, work out, exercise, perform, commit, to cause to exist, to produce.

To work for, earn by working, to acquire.

The work of showing a gracious, kind, compassionate, non-judgmental accepting attitude is demanding and will cost you emotionally, as well your time and your energy. The kind of work that God has called us to can only be done when we are in fellowship with Jesus. Fellowship with Jesus should produce compassion and generosity within a person.

Jesus warns them of the danger of loosing an opportunity to share in his work.

‘Night is coming when no one can work.’ Every one of us will have ‘a night when we cannot work.’ There will be times when we will need to receive the ministry this beggar received, not give it. There will be times in the will of God that our lives will be shrouded in the darkness of night, and we won’t have the resources to “work the works of him who sent him.’ We are those that have been sent to continue the works of Jesus, so when we can, we must reach out in love. Any lost opportunity to show gracious, kind, compassionate, non-judgmental accepting attitude to others when we can, is a loss of life itself.

We must remember that this was a Sabbath day, 9:14. For the Jews of Jesus’ day, especially for those who lived in Jerusalem, the Sabbath was a very restricted day, were all kinds of work was forbidden because of the traditions of the elders. Sometimes we are tempted to play it safe, we don’t want to rock the boat in case we might offend others. We allow the traditions and expectations of others to restrict how and when we show compassion, and the needy suffer because we are afraid to take the opportunities that God has given us. I once read of a church in Australia who provided the local brothel with a weekly gift of buns and cakes which in turn caused the sex workers to be curious about Jesus and feel valued. Wow!!!

Jesus reiterates his mission, ‘While I am in the world I am the light of the world.’

Jesus said this to establish a clear connection between the healing of this blind man and His claim to be the ‘Light of the world’ (John 18:12; cf. John 1:4; 12:46).

What Jesus previously claimed He now demonstrated by this miracle. Jesus the light of the world is seen through the deeds of compassion and grace that the church does in appropriate times and appropriate way.
prayer: Father help me see every opportunity to show compassion as an opportunity to share in the work of Jesus.
